description: This Zenodo deposit contains the electricity load profiles of 5,359 industrial company sites that were analysed in the paper "Electrical energy storage for industrial grid fee reduction – A large scale analysis" (Energy Conversion and Management, 2020, by Tiemann, Bensmann, Stuke and Hanke-Rauschenbach). The paper abstract states that the sites are companies in Germany and that each site's grid fee was computed under the German regulatory scheme with the prices of the connected grid operator; the deposit keywords add zip code and grid level, so the profiles appear to carry location and connection-level attributes (inferred from keywords). Version 1.0.1 was published on 9 October 2024 by Paul Hendrik Tiemann as one downloadable ZIP archive of about 297 MB, free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the deposit page has no description, so the time step, the year covered, the file format inside the archive and how company identities were anonymised are not stated on the page read; VEA, the energy buyers' association that supplied the data, is not explained there either. For simulation it is one of the largest open sets of real measured industrial demand, useful to build industrial load in distribution grid and national power system models, to test peak shaving, battery storage and demand response for factories, and to estimate how outages hit industrial consumers of different sizes. Related catalogue records include the SIELS simulated industrial load shapes, the South Korean factory electricity and demand response data and the NREL industrial facility combustion energy use data.
